aog_rate.reason: Rolling 28-day mean beat the current baseline on validation score (0.02790 vs 0.02893 RMSE) and review showed small fold biases, appropriate for noisy weakly autocorrelated AOG.

smx_rate.reason: Current recipe remained best; ridge alternative was materially worse. Fold RMSEs were stable around 0.027-0.031 with only modest bias swings.

umx_rate.reason: Conservative xgboost had the lowest validation score among tried UMX models (0.04920) and substantially reduced the current recipe's positive bias, with similar RMSE across folds.

cna_rate.reason: Rolling 28-day mean improved over current (0.01531 vs 0.01655) and reduced overforecast bias for this sparse low-rate series; review showed stable fold MAE.

program_live_legs.reason: Current recipe outperformed ridge and seasonal-naive alternatives by validation score; despite some fold/weekday bias, the tried simpler models had higher errors.

non_program_live_legs.reason: Conservative xgboost clearly improved over current and ridge (score 2.218 vs 2.625/2.552) with low fold-to-fold RMSE variation and reduced underbias.

daily_quote_count.reason: Current recipe had the best validation score; xgboost and ridge log-lag alternatives underforecasted later folds and were worse. Selected current despite residual bias because validation error was lower.

quote_multiplier.reason: Shrink-half curve was best of all bounded candidates (score 0.12265 vs 0.15181 current_lowess and 0.14884 constant_one) and was stable across folds.

conversion.reason: Isotonic curve slightly improved log loss and Brier over current exponential across all folds; constant curve was worse.
